title: The hand-over of the plan status between rwb-integration and rwb-case, and its batching, are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E2-002 sections 4 and 12 (the plan-status step of JOB-02 lists the open cases in rwb-case and calls RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor with batches of 500); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13 (the P3 row has no P2 cell and the P2 row has no P3 cell) and slides 14 and 16 (rwb-case and rwb-integration contracts); Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-11
section: 4 Flow; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story read the ACE plan status inside one service: it listed the open cases, called RestructurePlanQuery.statusFor with a list of account numbers in batches of 500, and wrote the status back through its own CasePlanStatus interface. In the target the ACE read belongs to rwb-integration, and no source says how the answer reaches rwb-case: the Architecture v5 connection matrix has neither a P3 to P2 call nor a P2 to P3 call, the integration contract for this legacy key publishes a per-case operation only, and no batch form of the read exists. The story therefore has to choose a direction and a batching rule, and a wrong choice changes the daily load on two services.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 13: the P3 row is blank in the P2 column and the P2 row is blank in the P3 column; slide 16 lists rwb-integration IN and OUT with no case operation; legacy RWB-E2-002 section 4 step 3 ('batches of 500 (assumed; DL11)') and section 12 ('Endpoint (new, recorded in additions)'); no batch operation named in any source read.
proposed: Keep the read with rwb-integration on its own base and have the plan-status step of DailyCaseRun call it once per case inside the readPlanStatus activity, with the page size and the bounded concurrency taken from the parameter rwb.ace.plan.batch-size = 500 and the timeout from rwb.ace.plan.timeout-ms = 2000; confirm with the P2 contract owner whether a batch operation is published in RWB-P2-E2002-CON.

title: No published operation reads a rule catalog row by rule ID and package version
source: Legacy RWB-E2-002 sections 4 and 12 (RuleCatalog.row(ruleId, packageVersion) returns action_text, owner_role and timer_spec); Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 15 T6 (rule_row stays as the parsed, queryable catalogue, read by rule ID and version); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (rule_row owner P7, basis TSD P3 v3 and the plan default ruling)
section: 4 Flow step 9; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 11 Data; 13 Solution plan
description: The route move needs the action text, the owner role and the timer spec of the rule that fired, and the legacy story read them from RuleCatalog by rule ID and package version. The ownership map puts rule_row, rule_package, rule_package_version and rule_test_case in rwb-decision (P7), so rwb-case must read them through the P7 contract, but neither the Architecture v5 contract lines nor the API specification names a catalog-row read: the published P7 paths are the rule-model read, the rule-version administration paths, the approvals and the decision log. The story names the call and leaves the path open.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 rwb-decision IN and OUT lists no rule-row read; ownership.json rule_row ruling (P7, TSD P4 v3 and TSD P3 v3 declare the table); legacy RWB-E2-002 section 12 `RuleRow RuleCatalog.row(String ruleId, String packageVersion)`; Temporal and Drools design slide 15 T6.
proposed: Publish the catalog-row read on /api/recovery/decision/v1 in the P7 contract story, returning action_text, owner_role, timer_spec, target queue code and outputs by rule ID and package version; until then the story reads the row through the contract fake and the KieBase answer.

title: The plan event map has no table code in LOV-REF-TABLE and no target table or column
source: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 3 (the plan event map rows are loaded) and section 13 (PlanEventMap, reference table); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T3.2 LOV-REF-TABLE and T3.1 reference_version, reference_row
section: 3 Preconditions; 11 Data; 13 Configuration and reference data
description: The plan event map turns an ACE plan status and a route state into the event code the case raises (BROKEN with PLAN_CURE_PERIOD to CURE_PERIOD_EXPIRED; BROKEN with any other route state to TREATMENT_BROKEN). The legacy story holds it as a versioned reference table. The target reference-data tables key every version by a table code, and LOV-REF-TABLE lists no code for this map, so the map cannot be loaded as reference data without adding a code or holding it somewhere else.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-002 sections 3, 5 and 13; TSD P3 v3 T3.2 LOV-REF-TABLE (PRODUCT, REGION, EXPOSURE_BAND, ROLE, TEAM, QUEUE, QUEUE_MEMBER, SERVICE_LEVEL, DOCUMENT_TYPE, DOCUMENT_CHECKLIST, RETENTION_CLASS, TEMPLATE, DELEGATION_LIMIT, PERMISSION, MASKING_RULE, PARTNER_USER, LEGAL_PERIOD, HOLIDAY, PRODUCT_PARAMETER, PARAMETER, ENTRY, EXCLUSION, ALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT, TRANSFER) with no plan event map code; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 reference_version and reference_row.
proposed: Add a table code for the plan event map to LOV-REF-TABLE in the reference-data story of the service and load its rows as reference_row under a reference_version, with one row per ACE status and route state pair; no map row in code.

title: The delivery path of a plan-status break to the data-quality console is not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E2-002 sections 5 and 7 (a break with product DP04 and a break with check Lists of values); FSD P3 v4 A2.28 AC-EXC-P3-028-01 (reconciliation break, reconciliation_result); _work/msr/plan/ownership.json (reconciliation_result owner P1)
section: 2 Business rationale; 5 Exception paths X1 and X3; 8 Business rules BR13; 19 Out of scope
description: Two legacy outcomes are breaks on the data-quality console: a plan the case holds that ACE no longer returns, and a status code that is not in the plan status list. The ownership map puts reconciliation_result in rwb-source-data (P1) and publishes no operation by which rwb-case can raise a break, and the legacy story wrote the break from inside the monolith. The story records the rejection in its own run and names the break, but the table and the call that put it in front of the data steward and the ACE team are open.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-002 section 5 X1 and X3 and section 7 AC3 and AC5; FSD P3 v4 A2.28 AC-EXC-P3-028-01 and AC-ALT-P3-028-02; ownership.json reconciliation_result (owner P1, Architecture v5 slide 41 and slide 44 JOB-04); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 lists no break operation on the P1 contract.
proposed: Publish a break operation on the rwb-source-data contract (product, check, key, detail, owner role) in the P1 contract story and have the plan-status step call it once per rejected or missing plan; until then the break is listed from the run summary of DailyCaseRun and no break row is written by rwb-case.

title: The gateway-bff composite route of the case record plan section is not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 (the gateway calls rwb-case and rwb-source-data in parallel and merges the answers) and slide 45; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-19; legacy RWB-E2-002 sections 4 step 8 and 15 (SCR-03 plan status panel, MSG-P2-008)
section: 4 Flow step 13; 12.1 REST operations provided; 13 Solution plan; 15 Screens and states
description: The case record plan section has two answers in the target: the live status of rwb-integration and the stored status of rwb-case. The Architecture states that gateway-bff composes composite screens from parallel one-hop calls but gives no route path, no merge rule (which answer wins when both are present, and what is shown when the live answer is missing or out of date), no field masking rule and no split of the 2 s budget for this screen.
evidence: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 note (two calls in parallel from gateway-bff, merge into the screen model) and slide 45; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-19 (gateway-bff composite route, no route given); no composite route document named in the sources read.
proposed: Publish the composite route for SCR-03 in RWB-PLT-N001-CON with its path, the two parallel calls, the merge rule (live answer wins, stored answer with MSG-P2-008 when the live one is missing or not live), the masking rule and the 2 s budget split.

title: The per-service database login name of rwb-case is not specified
source: Template and Rules v1 §R4 (one login per service) and §R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 notes (schema and login per service); TSD P3 Case and workflow v3 T2.5 (worker identity SY-CASEWF only)
description: Every service has its own login with grants on its own schema only, and DP-02 retires the shared recovery_svc login, but no source names the rwb-case login, its grant set or its secret reference. The migration, the connection pool and the contract-fake credentials of this story cannot name it, so the story uses a placeholder and the chart takes the name from a secret reference.
evidence: Template and Rules v1 §R4 and §R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 and slide 29 notes (one login per service, no name given); TSD P3 v3 T2.5 names SY-CASEWF and SY-RULES but no database login.
proposed: Allocate the login with the schema in the 19-schema list of the platform database story, derive the name from the schema, hold it in Key Vault and record it in the Service Catalog before the first deployment.
